title: Annual Large Bank Capital Requirements
summary: This Federal Reserve page provides a high-level overview of the capital requirements framework for large banks ($100B+ in assets), but functions primarily as a navigation hub linking to annual requirement PDFs rather than containing the actual requirements data itself. The framework requires minimum CET1 of 4.5%, a stress capital buffer (SCB) of at least 2.5%, and G-SIB surcharges of at least 1.0%.
key_points: Applies to bank holding companies, covered savings and loan holding companies, and U.S. intermediate holding companies with $100 billion or more in total consolidated assets
Total CET1 capital ratio requirement consists of: minimum 4.5% CET1, SCB requirement of at least 2.5%, and G-SIB surcharge of at least 1.0%
SCB requirements are determined from supervisory stress test results
Category IV firms generally not required to participate in supervisory stress test in odd years
PDFs with actual bank-specific capital requirements available for 2020-2025 (none for 2026 yet)
Last update to the page was September 30, 2025
why_it_matters: Large bank capital requirements are a core component of the financial system's safety net and affect how much capital banks must hold against potential losses. These requirements influence bank behavior, lending capacity, and systemic risk. The stress capital buffer framework directly ties capital requirements to adverse economic scenarios, creating a dynamic capital floor that expands when stress test results worsen.
market_structure_context: This page documents the regulatory framework governing bank capital adequacy. The SCB requirement creates a market-structure mechanism where bank capital requirements respond to stress test outcomes, which are tied to portfolio composition and risk exposures. The G-SIB surcharge ensures systemically important institutions hold additional capital. However, this page does not provide current period capital requirements—it is a methodology and linkage page.
